description: One-dimensional and two-dimensional arrays, searching, sorting and matrix basics in C

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct declaration of an integer array of 5 elements in C?
questions.explanation: The correct syntax for declaring an integer array of 5 elements is int arr[5].

questions.questionText: What is the index of the first element of an array in C?
questions.explanation: C arrays use zero-based indexing, so the first element has index 0.

questions.questionText: For int arr[5], what is the index of the last element?
questions.explanation: An array of 5 elements has indexes from 0 to 4.

questions.questionText: What is the total number of elements in int arr[10]?
questions.explanation: The declaration int arr[10] creates an array containing 10 elements.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int arr[5] = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}; printf("%d", arr[2]);
questions.explanation: arr[2] refers to the third element because array indexing starts from 0.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int arr[5] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}; printf("%d", arr[0] + arr[4]);
questions.explanation: arr[0] is 1 and arr[4] is 5, so their sum is 6.

questions.questionText: What happens to the remaining elements when int arr[5] = {1, 2}; is declared?
questions.explanation: When an array is partially initialized, the remaining elements are initialized to zero.

questions.questionText: Which loop is commonly used to traverse all elements of an array?
questions.explanation: A for loop is commonly used to access array elements sequentially.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int a[4] = {2, 4, 6, 8}; int sum = 0; for(int i = 0; i < 4; i++) sum += a[i]; printf("%d", sum);
questions.explanation: The sum is 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20.

questions.questionText: Which expression gives the number of elements in an array int arr[10]?
questions.explanation: For an actual array, dividing its total size by the size of one element gives the number of elements.

questions.questionText: What is the result of sizeof(int arr[10]) conceptually on a typical system where int is 4 bytes?
questions.explanation: If an int occupies 4 bytes, an array of 10 ints occupies 10 × 4 = 40 bytes.

questions.questionText: Which declaration represents a two-dimensional integer array with 3 rows and 4 columns?
questions.explanation: The declaration int arr[3][4] creates 3 rows and 4 columns.

questions.questionText: How many elements are present in int matrix[3][4]?
questions.explanation: A 3 × 4 matrix contains 3 × 4 = 12 elements.

questions.questionText: What is the correct way to access the element in the second row and third column of int matrix[3][4]?
questions.explanation: Rows and columns are zero-indexed, so the second row has index 1 and the third column has index 2.

questions.questionText: Which method is commonly used to find an element by checking array elements one by one?
questions.explanation: Linear search checks elements sequentially until the required element is found or the array ends.

questions.questionText: What is the main requirement for applying binary search efficiently to an array?
questions.optionB: The array must contain only positive numbers
questions.optionC: The array must have exactly 10 elements
questions.explanation: Binary search requires the data to be sorted so that the search space can be repeatedly divided.

questions.questionText: Which sorting algorithm repeatedly compares adjacent elements and swaps them if they are in the wrong order?
questions.explanation: Bubble sort repeatedly compares adjacent elements and swaps them when necessary.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int a[3] = {3, 1, 2}; int temp = a[0]; a[0] = a[1]; a[1] = temp; printf("%d %d %d", a[0], a[1], a[2]);
questions.explanation: The first two elements are swapped, resulting in 1 3 2.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int a[5] = {5, 10, 15, 20, 25}; printf("%d", *(a + 2));
questions.explanation: a + 2 points to the third element, so *(a + 2) gives 15.

questions.questionText: In C, the name of an array generally represents:
questions.optionA: The value of the last element
questions.optionB: A pointer to the first element in most expressions
questions.optionD: A pointer to the last element
questions.explanation: In most expressions, an array name decays to a pointer to its first element.
a[1][2] refers to the second row and third column, whose value is 6.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of the main diagonal of the matrix {{1,2,3},{4,5,6},{7,8,9}}?
questions.explanation: The main diagonal elements are 1, 5 and 9. Their sum is 15.

questions.questionText: Which condition correctly checks whether an element was found at index i during a linear search?
questions.explanation: The equality operator == is used to compare the array element with the search key.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int a[4] = {1, 2, 3, 4}; for(int i = 3; i >= 0; i--) printf("%d ", a[i]);
questions.explanation: The loop starts at index 3 and moves backward to index 0, printing 4 3 2 1.

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of linear search in the worst case for an array of n elements?
questions.explanation: In the worst case, linear search may check all n elements, so its time complexity is O(n).
